headline: TREK’s MCP/browser surface plus broad egress creates the main risk: prompt injection and cascading misuse are plausible, while direct data leakage and compliance risk are elevated by shared travel data and secrets handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: plano has broad network egress and an OpenAI-compatible API surface, while TREK uses browsers and MCP. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content is fed into plano or vice versa. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into plano prompts or tool inputs without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF either agent treats browser/MCP content as trusted instructions, the bridge becomes exploitable.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of browser/MCP text into prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages.
Require human review for any instruction-like content from TREK.
Restrict plano to read-only summarization of TREK outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano has broad network egress and touches logs/metrics/traces, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. If the pair shares a workspace or passes sensitive travel data through plano, exfiltration risk is substantial. The evidence does not prove a shared filesystem, so I do not call it critical.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservation data are forwarded into plano context, they can leave via plano's broad egress.
IF both agents are deployed on the same host with shared files, sensitive travel artifacts can be exposed.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of plano prompts and logs.
Separate storage for TREK uploads and plano inputs.
Rotate any API keys exposed to TREK immediately.
Disable outbound access from plano except required endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: plano is not multi-instance and has file/config surfaces, while TREK supports multiple collaborative instances and writes to travel.db, uploads, and logs. Overlapping mutable state is plausible if they share a host or workspace, but the profiles do not prove same-directory writes or locking absence, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database, state corruption becomes possible.
IF TREK collaborative sessions and plano config edits target the same files, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own directory.
Make plano config read-only during TREK sessions.
Back up shared files before concurrent use.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run lock file.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, and plano is an AI gateway/proxy that can route model outputs. If plano feeds generated content into TREK without verification, TREK may act on incorrect travel facts or recommendations. Because the pair can create an automated content-to-action chain, high is warranted.
conditions: IF plano output is used as authoritative input to TREK workflows, errors can cascade.
IF TREK auto-applies AI-generated itinerary changes, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a verification step before TREK accepts plano output.
Show source citations alongside any AI-generated travel advice.
Disable auto-apply for itinerary or reservation changes.
Log and review all cross-agent transformations.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while plano touches logs/metrics/traces and has broad egress. That combination raises compliance and residency concerns if regulated travel or identity data flows through plano; the profiles do not show matching controls, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF EU personal data or travel documents are routed through plano, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF TREK secrets are logged or forwarded by plano, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it between agents.
Keep regulated documents out of plano logs.
Confirm a DPA and residency policy for any personal data flow.
Redact email addresses and confirmation numbers before transfer.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
